implementation.module_data: Initial globals/constants use local VRAM whenever the bound runtime has an internal transfer queue; the bound memory module retains host backing for bootstrap.
implementation.descriptors: Scratch descriptors use local VRAM when local_thread_memory is enabled.
implementation.upload: Reuse the ISA staging slab and reserved native queue; preserve the caller recording and indirect heap. Upload initial module data once; subsequent GPU writes persist across kernels/queues.

host_stack_audit.note: Frame sizes are measured from compiler output; array-size reduction alone does not predict register spills. The initial overly strict minimum-delta assertion was corrected to check the actual frame and probe invariants.

validation.module_fixture: Both host/device placements; shared initialized/zero-valued globals and volatile constants; two kernels/queues, 16 updates/17 readbacks per placement, persistent state, full guards and stable allocations.

model_caveats: Native arms compare preserved old-state and candidate executables with identical kernels; ISA and scratch/private remain device-local in all native arms. Only module-data/scratch-descriptor placement and first-use upload implementation change.
Original L0 controls use the preserved production executable and production images under identical request/profile parameters.
Fixed 28-token prompt, natural76 greedy output, 5771 expert slots, no prefix reuse.
Ten warmups and five retained requests per process; engine decode excludes preparation and prefill.
Host delivery timing is not GPU timestamps; clocks are unlocked and OS caches remain populated.
Requested VRAM reserve is configuration, not continuously measured physical headroom.
first_model_note: The first complete bracket used the initial 4-KiB descriptor host buffer; the final bracket uses 256 bytes and uploader zero padding with identical GPU bytes. Both complete brackets are retained; no individual benefit is attributed to the stack change.

auto_cache_smoke.caveat: Startup availability is one host observation, not continuously measured physical headroom; one cold request is not a throughput benchmark.

limitations: One fixed prompt, host timings and unlocked clocks; no native GPU timestamps or broad PPL/long-context validation.
The native-versus-parent comparison combines module-data/descriptor placement and the shared first-use uploader; it does not isolate each component.
Indirect parameters, command buffers and the memory module retain their prior backing.
Linux frontend/GPU, dependency-aware barriers, hardware queues, unsupported variants, eventfd and pool trimming remain open.
Startup availability is not continuous physical headroom; existing preparation allowances require recalibration if the pack/queue topology grows.
